draft.title: Methods in biology
card: changes one factor on purpose and keeps the others the same. It suits questions about cause and effect.
looks for a relationship between two factors without changing either. It shows a link, but cannot show that one factor causes the other.
collects data in a natural setting, such as a creek or forest. It suits questions about organisms in their real environment, though conditions are harder to control.
uses a physical, mathematical or computer model to represent a system. It suits questions that are too large, slow, small or risky to test directly.
draft.remember: Match the method to the question: cause and effect, links, natural settings or systems too hard to test directly.

a.q: Which question is best answered by a controlled experiment?
opts: Does light change the rate of photosynthesis in pondweed?
Do areas with more trees also have more bird species?
How many frog species live along a river in Gippsland?
How might a virus spread through a city in ten years?
a.why: A controlled experiment changes one factor, light, and keeps the others the same, so it can test cause and effect. The tree and bird question suits a correlational study, because it only looks for a link.
a.clue: Which question lets you change one factor on purpose?

b.q: A researcher records the daily steps and resting heart rates of 200 adults and finds that more active adults have lower heart rates. What can she conclude?
opts: The two factors are linked, but this study cannot show cause
More steps cause a lower resting heart rate in adults
A lower resting heart rate causes adults to take more steps
There is no relationship between steps and heart rate
b.why: She measured two factors without changing either, so this is a correlational study. It shows a link, but it cannot show that one factor causes the other. Fitter adults could have other differences that explain the pattern.
b.clue: She did not change either factor.

a.best: Does light change the rate of photosynthesis in pondweed?

b.best: The two factors are linked, but this study cannot show cause
